newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain convicts ex-spy for leaking dirty war files.
newsitem.headline: Spain convicts ex-spy for leaking dirty war files.

text.p: Spain's central military court convicted a senior military intelligence officer on Thursday of leaking secret files on a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatist rebels.
The court sentenced Colonel Juan Alberto Perote, former head of covert operations, to seven years in prison for stealing secrets that affected state security.
The court said that Perote had stolen 1,200 documents from the Spain's military intelligence department CESID when he left his position in 1991.
The top secret files include some that are vital to state security and others that implicate the former Socialist government in the "dirty war" in which 28 people were killed.
The papers purportedly show that former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez and his associates set up undercover squads to combat separatist violence by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).

The scandal that broke when the papers were published in newspapers in 1995 led to a raft of resignations by top officials in the Socialist government and last year's election defeat of the long-ruling Gonzalez.
